pixel_reference: pixel centres; first centre west + half a pixel, north - half a pixel
name: CRISM mineral browse layers for the MarsWay EVA area
dataset: CRISM Specialized Browse Product Mosaics, MSL Gale Crater, 23 July 2012 (MTRDR prototypes)
instrument: Compact Reconnaissance Imaging Spectrometer for Mars (CRISM), Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter
credit: NASA/JPL/JHUAPL; mosaics by F. Seelos, K. Seelos, C. Viviano (CRISM team)
source_crs: Simple cylindrical, Mars 2000 sphere, centre (0, 0), 3072 px/deg = 19.295 m/px
project_crs: Mars 2000 sphere, Equidistant Cylindrical, centre lon 0 (metres)
registration: CRISM team warped each observation onto a CTX basemap (ENVI RST); registration to this terrain DEM is unverified; offsets may remain.

HYD.legend: Hydrated sulfates. R SINDEX2, G BD2100_2, B BD1900_2. Monohydrated sulfates green or yellow; polyhydrated sulfates magenta; other hydrated minerals blue.
HYD.coverage_note: Outside-mosaic and black browse pixels are transparent. Black pixels may reflect no coverage, dust, weak signal or the browse stretch floor, not mineral absence.

ALT.legend: Alteration minerals at Gale. R D2300, G SINDEX2, B BD1900_2. Hydrated sulfates green or blue-green; Fe/Mg clays red.
ALT.coverage_note: Outside-mosaic and black browse pixels are transparent. Black pixels may reflect no coverage, dust, weak signal or the browse stretch floor, not mineral absence.

limitations: Qualitative browse colours with a Gale-specific stretch. Brighter colour is a stronger spectral signal than elsewhere at Gale, not a percentage of mineral.
About 19.3 m source pixels, roughly 311 across the area. A 5 m output grid adds no detail; individual boxwork ridges are not resolved.
Dust hides minerals: a black or bland pixel does not mean the mineral is absent.
2012 prototype products, before the final PDS MTRDR release. Ice haze can add false blue.
